## Business overview

HDFC Bank is a Mumbai-headquartered bank and India's largest private sector lender by assets [E1]. It offers retail, personal and wholesale banking, cards, loans, investments and FASTag services [E42][E44][E46].

Scale and franchise:
- Deposits were ₹3,105,250 cr at Mar 2026 [F34].
- The bank serves about 100 million customers and adds 6–8 million a year [E81].
- It runs about 9,700 branches, close to 40% of them under five years old [E71].
- Its mobile app has over 60 million registered customers [E85].

Loan mix and merger effects:
- Retail is 52% of the loan mix, against a historical level of about 60% [E49].
- After the merger, liability penetration among home-loan customers rose from 36% to about 50% [E82].
- Mortgages are now offered from more than 7,800 locations [E79].

Revenue mix:
- Other income equals 65.7% of PBT, so non-interest streams are material to earnings [F43].

## Bull case

- The price implies only 4.6% growth, against a 10y profit CAGR of 19.8% [F51][F6].
- Lower borrowings (11% toward 5–6%) and a 40–50 bp cost-of-funds benefit could support margins [E48][E47].
- The latest-quarter operating margin of 15.5% is above the FY26 level of 11.8% [F30][F14].
- Asset quality is improving, with gross NPA down from 1.4% to 1.2% [F41][F39].
- Deposit growth of 14.4% outpaced FY26 loan growth of 12% [F35][E78]. Management also reports deposit market-share gains [E57].

## Bear case

- Growth has slowed: FY26 revenue grew 2.3% and latest-quarter profit grew 5.0% [F8][F28].
- ROE has fallen to 14.0%, below its 5y average of 15.8% [F18][F19].
- At 34%, CASA is below peers at about 40%, and incremental SA market share has flatlined [E68][E70].
- Leadership succession and earlier governance reviews remain unresolved [E36][E90].
- The stock is in a downtrend, with a 1y drawdown of 30.8% and FIIs cutting their stake by 7.02 pp [F101][F93][F68].
